study type: Retrospective analysis of repeated national surveys
cohort: Children (twins and singletons) under five years of age from 42 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, whose data were collected via 156 national surveys.
finding: Under-5 mortality rates are, on average, 3 times higher among twins than singletons in Sub-Saharan Africa, with low birth weight, non-use of cesarean section delivery, and lack of breastfeeding identified as key associated factors.
mod_finding: Non-use of cesarean section delivery was identified as a significant factor associated with increased excess mortality risks among twins.
cross-section timing: Data from national surveys conducted between 1986 and 2016
